description: Imports Iterable marketing-automation data: campaigns and campaign metrics, channels, message types, templates, lists and list membership, user profiles, and message/engagement events.

transports.purpose: Export-job result files are downloaded from pre-signed object-store URLs returned by the Iterable export API, fetched deliberately WITHOUT the Iterable API key (with_token=False). The host is not named anywhere in the connector; only the fact that the URL is pre-signed and expirable is visible.

baseUrl.resolution: per-file pre-signed URL taken from files[].url in the GET /api/export/{jobId}/files response

artifacts: Iterable async export jobs (created by POST /api/export/start, addressed by jobId) for the `users` and `events` streams
continuity.customerSideAccrual: Nothing accrues in the customer's Iterable account from us pausing: no log, slot, or change table is retained on our behalf. The only server-side residue is export jobs that were already submitted; if the connector stops mid-job they remain enqueued/running in the customer's Iterable export-job queue and occupy their export concurrency until Iterable finishes or expires them.
continuity.ourSideLoss: Nothing is lost by pausing per se — export windows are re-requested from the stored cursor. Two second-order costs: (a) a long pause makes the next window large, and an export exceeding Iterable's 100GB cap returns exportTruncated, forcing the connector to halve the window and resubmit repeatedly; (b) within an in-flight job the pre-signed result URLs expire (HTTP 403 'Request has expired'), which the connector handles by re-fetching the current file page for fresh URLs.
continuity.notes: The connector does not cancel its export jobs on shutdown. It cancels them on the NEXT startup instead: `open()` calls all_resources(..., should_cancel_running_jobs=True), which enumerates GET /api/export/jobs and issues DELETE /api/export/{jobId} for every job in `running` or `enqueued` state. So orphaned jobs persist for the whole pause and are reaped only when we come back. A single job is also given up to MAX_WAIT_SECONDS = 24h to complete before ExportJobTimeoutError, and at most MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS = 4 run at once.

authTierRationale: The connector offers exactly one credential mode. EndpointConfig.credentials is a single-member discriminated union of ApiKey (a subclass of the CDK's AccessToken, discriminator 'Private App Credentials'), whose only user-supplied field is `access_token`, titled 'API Key' and marked secret. The connector's ConnectorSpec sets oauth2=None and TokenSource is constructed with oauth_spec=None, so there is no OAuth path at all — no client registration, no refresh token, no hosted control plane involvement. The user pastes one self-serve Iterable API key, which the CDK sends verbatim as the `Api-Key` header. That is T1_SIMPLE.

unionMisfits.description: The `users` and `events` streams do not read an HTTP collection at all; they drive a three-phase async export job and there is no PullSpec kind for that. Phase 1 POSTs /api/export/start with a JSON body ({dataTypeName, startDateTime, endDateTime, outputFormat: application/x-json-stream}) and receives {jobId}. Phase 2 polls GET /api/export/{jobId}/files with exponential backoff (1s doubling to a 300s cap, hard ceiling 24h) reading `jobState` from the envelope until `completed`; a `completed` job carrying exportTruncated=true is a FAILURE signal that makes the connector halve the date window and resubmit, recursively, down to a 1-second floor. Phase 3 pages the RESULT FILE LIST — not the records — from the same GET /api/export/{jobId}/files by sending startAfter=<last filename of the previous page>, terminating when a page returns fewer than MAX_FILES_PER_PAGE=10 files. The actual records are then streamed as JSONL from per-file pre-signed URLs on a DIFFERENT host, fetched with the Iterable API key deliberately suppressed (with_token=False), with a 403 'Request has expired' handler that re-fetches the current file page for fresh URLs. Forcing this into `{kind: http, path: /api/export/start, paginator: none}` (as this document does, for schema conformance) loses every operationally significant fact: the poll loop, the truncation-driven window bisection, the file-list cursor, and the second unauthenticated transport. Note also that startAfter is record_cursor-shaped but over file objects rather than data records, and its `hasMore` is implicit in page size.

resultFetch.onExpiry: re-request the current file page (same startAfter) for fresh URLs

unionMisfits.description: The campaigns paginator is page-number based on the request side (page=1,2,3... with pageSize=1000) but its STOP signal is the presence of an envelope field: the loop continues while the response body's `nextPageUrl` is non-null and breaks when it is null. The URL is never followed and no token is extracted from it, so this is neither `next_url` nor `cursor`. The schema's `page` variant accepts terminateOn: envelope_flag but provides no field in which to name WHICH envelope field carries the flag, nor the polarity (continue-while-present vs stop-while-present). Two connectors with opposite polarity would serialize identically.

proposedShape.envelopeFlagSemantics: continue while the field is present and non-null

unionMisfits.description: campaigns is incremental with NO server-side incremental parameter. The connector sorts descending (sort=-updatedAt), reads pages from the top, and breaks out of the loop client-side the moment a campaign's updatedAt is <= the checkpointed cursor; the new cursor is the max updatedAt seen. The schema's incrementalParam assumes the filter is pushed down to the API, and there is no way to express 'sorted server-side, terminated client-side' — which matters, because the cost model (full first page every poll, early exit) and the failure mode (a source that ignores or reorders `sort` silently truncates the sync) are completely different from a pushed-down filter.

campaign_metrics has no independent path of its own: to build its request it first fully re-paginates /api/campaigns, filters those campaigns by state (pre-launch -> skip; in-progress -> always fetch; final -> fetch only when max(updatedAt, endedAt) falls inside a [cursor - 15 days, now] lookback window), then fans out /api/campaigns/metrics in batches of <=80 campaignId query params with a hardcoded startDateTime of the epoch, sleeping 6s between batches for a 10 req/min limit. The response is CSV, not JSON. The schema has no notion of a parent-stream-derived request set, of a per-request id batch size, or of a CSV response body, and `incrementalParam` is misleading here because the date param sent is constant while the real incrementality lives entirely in which campaign ids get selected.

proposedShape.parentSelection: campaignState-based, with a 15-day lookback on max(updatedAt, endedAt) for campaigns in a final state

unionMisfits.description: list_users is a parent-scoped stream whose backfill page cursor is a LIST ID, not an offset or token: each invocation of the backfill task lists /api/lists, sorts the ids, bisects to find the next id after the checkpointed one, fetches exactly ONE list's users, checkpoints that id, and sleeps to respect a 5 req/min limit. The response is not JSON at all — /lists/getUsers returns newline-delimited bare user ids, which the connector pairs with the list id to synthesize documents; there is no records path and no envelope. `pathPlaceholders` cannot express this because the scoping value arrives as a query param derived from a sibling stream, and `paginator: none` understates it: there IS resumable progress, it is just keyed on parent identity.

proposedShape.parentOrder: ascending, one parent per task invocation

resumeCursor.lookup: bisect into the sorted parent id list

proposedShape.partialFailurePolicy: after 3 transport-level retries, or a persistent HTTP 500 with the generic error body, skip the list and checkpoint whatever was captured

unionMisfits.description: `events` is one Flow collection but 150 independently-cursored subtasks: the CDK's open_binding is handed a dict of fetch_changes keyed realtime_<eventType> and lookback_<eventType> (50 event types x 2) plus a fetch_page dict keyed by event type, each with its own cursor in ResourceState. `users` has the same shape at 2 subtasks. The schema's stream model assumes at most one incremental cursor per stream, so `cursorField: createdAt` is true of each subtask but hides that there are 150 of them advancing independently — which is the dominant fact for both quota and lag reasoning.

legSemantics.realtime: cursor starts at open time and advances to `now`
legSemantics.lookback: identical query with a 1-hour horizon subtracted from the end bound, to catch Iterable's eventually-consistent late arrivals; deduplicated against the realtime leg via the CDK's emitted_changes_cache

unionMisfits.description: The users stream's primary key is chosen at runtime from the endpoint config, not fixed by the connector: project_type Email-based -> key ['/email'] (model UsersWithEmails), UserID-based or Hybrid -> key ['/itblUserId'] (model UsersWithIds). The schema has no way to express a config-dependent key, so the emitted value ['/email'] is only correct for one of the three settings.

The connector marks list_users with disable=True, meaning the binding is discovered but not enabled by default. The schema has no per-stream enabled-by-default field, so a consumer reading this document would turn on a binding the connector authors deliberately ship off (it is the one with a 5 req/min limit and 80-minute responses).

The second transport entry is a poor fit for `role: sidecar`. A sidecar in the v2 sense is a distinct SERVICE the user configures (e.g. a schema registry); here it is the same logical data path — result files of the primary's own export jobs — served from per-file pre-signed URLs on an unnamed host, with authentication deliberately OMITTED. There is no config, no base URL, and no credential; modeling it as a sidecar implies a user-visible second endpoint that does not exist.

proposedShape.purpose: download pre-signed result objects produced by the primary transport
proposedShape.note: unauthenticated by design; URLs expire and are re-minted by re-requesting the producing endpoint

abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No connector code sets any static request header. Every call goes through http.request / request_stream / request_lines with only params, a JSON body, or a timeout; the only header the CDK injects is the auth header. Nothing establishes a required Accept or Content-Type at this layer, so the field is null rather than invented.
abstained.transports[0].spec.apiVersionPinning: There is no version header, version query param, or version path segment. The base URL's trailing `/api` is a namespace, not a version — Iterable's own docs call these v1 endpoints, but nothing in the connector encodes that, so it is not extracted.
abstained.transports[1].spec.baseUrl.value: The result-file host is never named in the connector. Only `file.url` from the response is used, so whether it is S3, GCS, or an Iterable-fronted CDN is not determinable from source. Recorded as `resolved` with the resolution described rather than guessing a host.
abstained.execution.continuity.resumeWindow: Nothing in the connector encodes how long an Iterable export job or its pre-signed result URLs remain valid. MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (24h) is OUR patience for a single job, not the source's retention. The pre-signed URL expiry is handled reactively via a 403 'Request has expired' string match with no stated TTL. There is therefore no evidence for a resume window, and inventing one would be a data-loss-shaped guess.
abstained.streams[5].cursorField: list_users has no cursor. It is registered with only fetch_page (a backfill task) and no fetch_changes, and its ResourceState carries only a Backfill entry. Its backfill page cursor is a parent list id, not a record field, so there is no cursorField to report.
abstained.streams[5].pull.backfill.recordsPath: /lists/getUsers does not return JSON. The connector reads the response with request_lines and treats each line as a bare user id string, synthesizing {list_id, user_id} documents. There is no envelope and no records path.
abstained.streams[7].cursorField.serverSide: campaign_metrics keeps a connector-side datetime cursor (advanced to `now` each sweep, read back with a 15-day lookback) but that cursor is never sent to the API — startDateTime is hardcoded to the epoch date. There is no record field acting as a cursor, so cursorField is null; the incremental behaviour is entirely in which campaign ids are selected.
abstained.streams[7].pull.backfill: campaign_metrics is registered with fetch_changes only and its initial_state has no Backfill entry, so there is no separate historical sweep. It is not a snapshot either (no tombstone, keyed on /id), so `snapshot` is left null rather than misfiled.
abstained.streams[8].primaryKey: Emitted as ['/email'] only because that is what the checked-in discover snapshot shows for the test config. The real key is chosen at runtime from `project_type` (Email-based -> /email, UserID-based and Hybrid -> /itblUserId). See the config_dependent misfit; treat the emitted value as one of three possibilities, not a fact.
abstained.streams[8].pull.*.paginator: The `users` stream does not paginate an HTTP collection, so no paginator classification applies. Emitted as {type: none} for schema conformance; the real resumption mechanism (a startAfter file-list cursor inside the export-job flow) is in unionMisfits[0]. Do not read {type: none} here as 'one request returns everything'.
abstained.streams[9].pull.*.paginator: Same as users: `events` drives export jobs, not a paginated collection. {type: none} is a schema-conformance placeholder; see unionMisfits[0].
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.recordsPath.forExports: Export results are JSONL streamed from pre-signed URLs, one JSON document per line with no envelope, so there is no records path for users or events.
abstained.streams[*].incrementalParam: No stream sends a generic incremental query parameter. campaigns filters client-side after a server-side sort; campaign_metrics sends a constant epoch startDateTime; users and events send startDateTime/endDateTime in a POST JSON body to /export/start, which is a job submission parameter rather than a collection filter. Mapping any of these onto incrementalParam would misrepresent where the filtering happens.
abstained.discovery: Null by design: streamMode is static. The connector ships a fixed list built by all_resources(); the only config-driven variation is which users model is used and the fan-out over the 50-member EventTypes enum, neither of which queries the customer's schema.
abstained.streams[*].schedules.cronDefaults: Only list_users ships a non-empty default cron ('55 23 * * *'). Every other binding leaves ResourceConfigWithSchedule.schedule at its CDK default of empty string, so no cron is reported for them. Users may set one per binding; that is a user choice, not a connector fact.
